Facts: The case involves the Maharashtra Agricultural Lands (Ceilings on Holdings) Act, 1961, which came into force on January 26, 1962. The constitutional validity of the Act was challenged in the High Court and the High Court held that the provisions of the Act, other than s.28, were measures of agrarian reform and were protected by Art.31A of the Constitution. However, s.28 was held to be violative of Art.14 of the Constitution. In 1964, the Constitution (17th Amendment) Act was passed, as a result of which the 1961 Act, including s.28, was included in the Ninth Schedule. The 1961 Act was amended by various Maharashtra Acts, namely Act of 1968, of 1968, of 1969 and of 1970. The constitutional validity of the 1961-Act as amended by the various Maharashtra Acts was again challenged but the High Court upheld the validity of the Act as amended on the ground that it was protected by Arts.1A and 31B of the Constitution.

Issues: The main issue in this case is whether the various amendments to the Act of 1961 were protected by Art.31B.

Statute: The Maharashtra Agricultural Lands (Ceilings on Holdings) Act, 1961, as amended by various Maharashtra Acts, namely Act of 1968, of 1968, of 1969 and of 1970.

Ratio of the decision: The court held that the various amendments to the Act of 1961 were not protected by Art.31B, but they are, however, protected by Art.3A of the Constitution.

Ruling by Present Court (Decision): The court dismissed the appeal to this Court.

Conclusion: The court found that the various amendments to the Act of 1961 were not protected by Art.31B, but they are, however, protected by Art.3A of the Constitution. The court also found that the inclusion of the Act or Regulation in the Ninth Schedule would protect not only the principal Act or Regulation which is included in the Ninth Schedule but also the amendments which have made therein till the date of its inclusion in the Ninth Schedule, even though the constitutional amendment by which the Act or Regulation is included in the Ninth Schedule refers only to the principal Act or Regulation and not to the amendments thereof.
